L31·N2398unmasked layer
Fires on the *separator* token inside long digit strings — colons in clock times, commas in thousand-separated numbers, spaces/letters within ID/account numbers — while the same slot filled by a period (e.g. "p. iv", "10.1.0", "dec. 31st") drives it strongly negative; it essentially encodes "which delimiter goes between these numbers, not a period".

L31·N5021unmasked layer

L31·N13110unmasked layer
Mostly a diffuse "next-word-context" neuron: it peaks on ordinary mid-sentence tokens in informal web/blog prose (determiners, numbers, brand/noun fragments like "pay", "company", "will", "three", "2017") with no clear semantic theme, while being strongly *negatively* driven by the token immediately preceding "designed" ("specifically designed", "cleverly designed", "are designed") — i.e. it appears to encode a prediction that the next word is *not* "designed".
